heading: `where` clauses
text:
### `where` clauses [RLOW.5.5]

A `where` clause compiles to a beta-node join test — a
boolean expression tree over the pattern's bound slots
([IRET.7.5]): the token passes only when
the expression evaluates true.

**A conjunct may leave the join test only when it is decided.** The compiler
may compile a conjunct as an alpha test ([IRET.6.4]), and the loader may probe
on one as the join's index key ([IRET.7.5.1]), only when every slot it reads is
non-nullable and it cannot raise by the declared types of its operands, read
without narrowing ([LNUL.5.2]). A decided conjunct answers only `true` or
`false`, and a `false` decides the `where` wherever it is evaluated
([LNUL.4.2]). Taking it first therefore changes neither the fault the `where`
yields nor, for a negated pattern, whether it blocks. A conjunct that could
answer `null` or raise could change both, and stays in the join test.

alloy.name: iret_9_6__v5_lie_breaks_hoisting
alloy.note: WHY THE ARTEFACT MUST NOT LIE: a hoisted conjunct over a value the artefact lied about raises its EngineError alone and blocks the `no` pattern, where the whole `where` is false.

alloy.name: rlow_5_5__decided
alloy.note: A decided conjunct: it cannot raise by its declared types and its slot is not nullable -- what an alpha test or an index anchor may be.

alloy.name: rlow_5_5__v5_hoist_sound
alloy.note: HOISTING AND PROBING ARE SOUND for an artefact that does not lie: filters on decided conjuncts leave the decision of a positive and of a `no` pattern, and the record, unchanged. Admitting a nullable filter breaks it (TEETH). V5 as stated by [LNUL.4.2] and [IRET.9.5]: a false decides wherever it stands; otherwise the faults resolve by kind, then by the fields of the record (T2I); the evaluation order is free.

idris.name: rlow_5_5__guard_at
idris.note: The guard at one positive node, on the fact looked up at its position: alpha tests on the fact, join tests against its prefix, and the rest of the guard. Its own function so that a proof can reduce it by rewriting the lookup alone.

idris.name: rlow_5_5__guard_from
idris.note: The guard: every positive node's alpha tests on its fact and join tests on its prefix.

idris.name: rlow_5_5__fact_at
idris.note: The fact at a position of a token from a front: what the guard's lookup finds.

idris.name: rlow_5_5__nth_append
idris.note: The fact at the position after a prefix.

idris.name: rlow_5_5__prefix_of
idris.note: The prefix of a token from a front is the front's token: what the guard's `take i` reads.

idris.name: rlow_5_5__take_append
idris.note: The prefix of its own length.

idris.name: rlow_5_5__guard_from_node
idris.note: One node's guard is the same under alphas of one shape, given the rest at every position.

idris.name: rlow_5_5__guard_from_same
idris.note: The guard a chain lowers to decides alike under alphas of one shape.
